title: Process for updating domain metadata
body:
What's the right method for suggesting or requesting an edit to the `agency` or `organization` field of the [domain](https://github.com/cisagov/dotgov-data/blob/main/current-federal.csv) [exports](https://github.com/cisagov/dotgov-data/blob/main/current-full.csv)?  

In particular, there's two scenarios:  
* Simple normalizing.  In these cases, there's just some various in formatting or trivial naming differences that would be good to make consistent so that the data is cleaner.  Here's [two](https://github.com/cisagov/dotgov-data/blob/main/current-full.csv#L3980-L3982) [examples](https://github.com/cisagov/dotgov-data/blob/main/current-full.csv#L3963-L3964).  I would _think_ that these edits could be made without needing to bother the domain owner.  
* An `agency` or `organization` field is incorrect and should be changed.  There's some items where we'll come across mistakes in the data and it would be good to send in the corrected info and there be some means by which it can be run by the domain owner for an okay, and then updated.

body: FHFA has requested that we add pki.fhfa.gov, dc081.fhfa.gov, and va081.fhfa.gov to the OCSP/CRL list as pki.fhfa.gov is used solely for CRL information. title: StatDNS uses this dataset for statistical purposes

[StatDNS](https://www.statdns.com) is a DNS research project publishing monthly TLD zone files statistics highlighting the deployment of DNSSEC and IPv6 within the top-level domains.

Since .gov data has been made public, I have been processing the zone file dump to include the results in our monthly reports.

However, I noticed that despite the CSV files being updated on a regular basis, the gov.txt file hasn't been updated in 6+ months now. Is there any plan to update it on a more regular basis, or to publish it on ICANN's CZDS service?

title: Update zone file post-registry transition
body:
We've been doing silent updates to the zone file, but this one merits a PR since it drastically slims the size and complexity of the file. 

We've moved to our new registry and authoritative DNS operator ([Cloudflare](https://sam.gov/opp/84b13553be9643f6bd143480a4567352/view)), which performs DNSSEC signing on the fly. This removes NSEC and RRsig records from our zone file.

title: 107: CI to push automated gov.txt updates from CZDS API
body:
Resolves #107 - Creates GitHub Action workflow that daily pulls .gov zone file from CZDS API and pushes zone file contents to gov.txt if a diff is found. Script also allows for manually running workflow once it is merged to main.

Workflow currently triggered on push to es/107-zone-file-script for testing and demo purposes. This configuration will be removed once the branch is merged to main and it is confirmed to successfully run on main.

### Testing Locally (Requires an ICANN account)
1. In the command line, run `./scripts/download_zone_file.sh <ICANN_email> <ICANN_password>`. If you need an account to test, message @erinysong and I can provide you testing credentials.
2. The script should download and unzip the .gov zone file, resulting in an updated gov.txt

### Testing on GitHub Actions
Until this PR is pushed to main, this workflow cannot be run manually and for testing purposes is run on any push or PR to this branch (this is admittedly not the most ideal way to test and will be deleted later to do more thorough testing with the manual workflow option after merging). Make any temporary push to the branch and check for GitHub Actions to run the **Update gov.txt from CZDS API zone file** action. The action should successfully run.

title: Update gov.txt directly from zone
body:
In #107, we updated gov.txt (a copy of the zone file) each day from the version we [publish each day to CZDS](https://get.gov/posts/2022-09-14-making-infrastructure-less-invisible/#publishing-the-.gov-zone-file). Instead of pulling once daily from a copy, we should pull from our DNS provider, Cloudflare.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Get read-only API token from Cameron
- [x] Decide if we want to strip the zone file's comment header (the order of this file is also slightly different than CZDS)  - as of July 8/2024, the zone file currently matches Cloudflare's zone file format rather than CZDS's
- [x] gov.txt is updated daily via this new source
  - [x] Merge every 24 hours 
- [x] [ADR](https://github.com/cisagov/dotgov-data/blob/main/docs/architecture/0001-automated-zone-file-updates.md) is updated with any necessary changes based on this work

### Additional Context
It's recommended that you fork the dotgov-data repo for this work.

We intend to eventually poll more frequently than 24 hours since the provenance of the data is the real source. In this issue, the goal is to simply replace where we're sourcing.

title: Legislative Branch Inconsistency
body:
I noticed that some sites are listed as "The Legislative Branch" in the organization field, e.g. 
    https://g0vology.us/?search=agency%3A%22The+Legislative+Branch%22

However others have something other than "Legislative Branch". For example one agency listed is "The United States Senate", which is of course a component of the Legislative Branch, e.g. https://g0vology.us/?search=agency%3A%22United+States+Senate%22 

In all, there are `91` cases, where `Domain type == "Federal - Legislative"` but the `Agency` is *NOT* `"The Legislative Branch` they are "generally"[1] situations where the `Organization name` field seems to be in the exact same as the `Agency` field - e.g. You could replace the `Agency` value with "The Legislative Branch" and not lose any information.

[1] There are `13` cases where this is not quite the case and might take a bit more research to consider fixing:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/533589e7-e931-4ab6-ba7d-d96ee630eb60)

However, some of those seem like very close, e.g. "United States Senate" and "US Senate" or "Open World   Leadership Center" vs. "The Open World Leadership Center".

title: ci: SHA-pin third-party Actions across both workflows
body:
Replaces 5 tag references in `.github/workflows/` with commit SHAs, with the resolved tag/branch as a trailing comment.

## Changes (2 files, 5 references)

- `actions/checkout@v2` and `@v4` to resolved SHAs (`v2.7.0`, `v4.3.1`)
- `denoland/setup-deno@main` to SHA at current head of main
- `githubocto/flat@v3` to SHA at v3.4.0 (2 occurrences in flat.yml)

The `denoland/setup-deno@main` change is the most material: as a branch ref it can shift any time `denoland` updates main, which makes the dotgov-data build non-deterministic. SHA-pinning to the current head locks in the contract.

## Why

Same supply-chain hardening posture as the wider community response after CVE-2025-30066 (the `tj-actions/changed-files` compromise in March). A commit SHA is immutable; tags and branches are not.

YAML validated locally with `yaml.safe_load`.

title: Viewer initialization fails on forks after footer simplification
body:
## Problem

The data viewer stops during initialization on staging and fork GitHub Pages URLs. `applyRepoContext()` writes to `footer-nonproduction-note`, but that element was removed by #164. The resulting null dereference prevents CSV discovery and table initialization.

## Reproduction

Load current `index.html` with a non-production repository URL, for example `https://example.github.io/dotgov-data/`. Initialization raises:

```text
TypeError: Cannot set properties of null (setting 'hidden')
```

Reproduced from `04d6a886c3c6c33905bfd67e68a1b5ab45779f4e`. Production URLs bypass the failing branch. The same error also prevents the missing-CDN-library message from appearing on forks.

## Expected behavior

Remove the stale footer-element access while retaining the non-production banner, title and production-note handling. Forks should proceed to CSV discovery, or show the existing library-load error when dependencies are unavailable.

title: Fix data viewer startup on non-production deployments
body:
## Summary

Remove the stale `footer-nonproduction-note` access left after #164. Non-production deployments now finish initialization while retaining the warning banner, hostname title and hidden production-only footer note.

Fixes #165.

## Testing

- `node --test tests/viewer-startup.test.mjs`: **8 passed**. Four fail on unchanged main.
- Additional Chromium checks load the actual page with its pinned Tabulator/PapaParse libraries and fixture CSVs. Table startup, global search and clearing filters pass for production, canonical GitHub Pages, staging and fork URLs. Both non-production URLs fail before the fix.
- The committed startup tests use Node's built-in runner with no added dependencies. They exercise initialization, not table rendering; the Chromium checks separately cover rendering.
- All browser requests were intercepted with local fixtures. No live CSV or API requests were made during testing.
